key_insight: A generative LLM can be used at test time to iteratively refine a user query (via feedback on a small set of retrieved documents), producing a task-adapted query embedding that substantially improves zero-shot search and classification without retraining the embedding model.
problem_solved: Fixed pre-trained embedding models often fail on challenging zero-shot retrieval/classification because they can't adapt to specific task nuances; this method enables on-the-fly adaptation of query representations to the target task.
method: Use a base embedding model to retrieve a small set of top documents for the original query.
Prompt a generative LLM to analyze those documents and produce a refined query, clarifying instructions, or an embedding-affecting augmentation.
Recompute the embedding for the refined query (optionally apply iterative refinement) and rerun retrieval/classification—no embedding model fine-tuning required.
impact: Provides a practical, low-cost way to boost zero-shot retrieval and classification performance by combining LLM reasoning with existing embeddings at test time—useful for practitioners who need better results without model retraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Query → embedding → initial retrieval → LLM feedback → refined query → re-embedding → improved results
Embedding-space illustration: original query vector vs. refined vector showing movement toward relevant document cluster
Before/after performance chart (e.g., precision@k or ROC/PR curves) comparing base embeddings vs. LLM-refined embeddings
Prompt + LLM callout card: example prompt and sample LLM-produced refinement to show how guidance looks
paper_title: Task-Adaptive Embedding Refinement via Test-time LLM Guidance
paper_authors: Ariel Gera, Shir Ashury-Tahan, Gal Bloch, Ohad Eytan, Assaf Toledo
